1.notes:
CPBFFL ICYMI — WEEK 1

Week 1 is done. A few of you looked ready for football. A few of you looked like you drafted on a toilet and forgot to flush.

Matt scored the most. Erik scored the least. Tony and Sam each had a win on the bench. Jake got his rivalry lead beaten out of him. Week 2 is here—set a lineup that doesn't make me want to file a welfare check.

Brian Corrigan|Erik Mannarino.title: GAME OF THE WEEK: ASHTON PLENTY, ERIK EMPTY
Brian Corrigan|Erik Mannarino.body:
Brian 130.40, Erik 101.86 | Brian leads 11–7

No hangover for the defending champ. Jeanty put up 33, Amon-Ra 28, and the Jaguars defense 15 after getting to play against what looked like a JV offense. Brian had a few guys do absolutely nothing, and it didn't matter.

Erik reached for the Rams defense early just to watch it give him negative points. Taylor gave him 25. McBride gave him 24. The rest of the team acted like they'd just gotten off a flight from Australia and were too fucking tired to play.

Deebo scored 18 on Erik's bench while Quentin Johnston scored 3 in his flex. That was stupid, but don't start with the “if I played Deebo” bullshit. Brian won by almost 29. Erik had the lowest score in the league and got his ass kicked on the biggest stage of the week.

Paul Deutsch|Shawn Smutak.title: ZAY POWERS, SMUTAK'S LIGHTS OUT
Paul Deutsch|Shawn Smutak.body:
Paul 154.80, Shawn 132.81 | Paul adds to his historical H2H lead

Dart scored 26. Zay scored 29 before his hamstring gave out. Pittsburgh's defense scored 20. Ja'Marr Chase scored 3, and Paul still had the second-highest total in the league. That's a fucking annoying team to lose to.

Jefferson put up 31 and Olave 28 for Shawn. Four other starters couldn't even get to double digits. Hampton gave him 8, Dobbins 3, and Jameson 8. JJ and Olave were trying to keep the boat afloat while the rest of those assholes took turns punching holes in it.

Paul beat Shawn last year, too. Apparently Deutsch ruining my Sunday is now league history.

Steve Cegelka|Tony Yokiel.title: BOSTON ON THE BENCH, TONY IN THE LOSS COLUMN
Steve Cegelka|Tony Yokiel.body:
Steve 118.11, Tony 111.12 | Steve adds another H2H win

“The Bye Week” came back and immediately scored the third-lowest total in the league. Puka scored 12. DeVonta 8. Adams 5. Kittle 3. Houston's defense went negative. Fucking inspiring stuff, Tony.

Steve had his own collection of useless starts—Waddle 1, Terry 3, Pollard 4—but Henry ran for 36, JSN scored 27, and Bucky added 20. His best guys showed up. That's all it took. Steve is a one-time champion; Tony has three titles and somehow still couldn't find the winning flex play on his own bench.

Tony was buried heading into Monday, and Kenneth Walker came out blazing for 39. It nearly worked. You know what would have worked? Starting Denzel Boston's 14 instead of Adams's 5. With the actual unrounded points, Tony wins by 2.31 on that swap. The winning lineup was sitting on his bench while the three-time champ watched his season start 0–1.

Matt Rennert|Michael Clark.title: GIBBS ME THAT
Matt Rennert|Michael Clark.body:
Matt 156.79, Mike 121.56 | Matt leads their owner-era series 1–0

I picked Matt to win the championship. He responded with the highest score in Week 1, because now he's going to be even more unbearable. Gibbs scored 34, Monty 28, and Javonte 24. Gibbs and Montgomery aren't even teammates anymore and they're still finding ways to fuck up someone else's Sunday.

Mike got 37 out of Josh Allen and still lost by 35. CMC gave him 13. Denver's defense went negative. Kincaid scored 18 on the bench while Fannin scored 4, but that wasn't going to save Mike either.

And no, we're not counting some old franchise's games to pretend these two had a rivalry. Matt and Mike were 0–0 as owners before this. Matt's first entry in their H2H book is a beating.

Jake Stacy|John DeBrouse.title: CHRISTIAN GIGAWATSON, JAKE IN THE SHITTER
Jake Stacy|John DeBrouse.body:
John 146.87, Jake 106.46 | H2H tied 6–6

Jake came in leading this rivalry 6–5. John tied it up by beating him by more than 40 fucking points.

Swift put up 33, Likely 27, and Watson 35. John even had Jalen Coker's 36 sitting on his bench. Jake should thank him for that much mercy.

Lamar scored 28 for Jake. After that? A.J. Brown 5, Rashee Rice 9, LaPorta 9, and Wan'Dale 8. Five single-digit starters overall. Jake was the second-lowest scoring team in the league and managed to turn a close historical rivalry into a Week 1 public execution.

Reid Masters|Sam Young.title: GHOST IN LOVELAND, MONANGAI IN THE WRONG PLACE
Reid Masters|Sam Young.body:
Reid 138.55, Sam 128.06 | Reid leads 4–0

Reid did what Reid always does. Lawrence scored 25, Bijan 31, DJ Moore 22, and the team had enough everywhere else to absorb Pickens's 5 and Dowdle's 4. Four meetings with Sam. Four wins.

Sam got 36 from Caleb while the Bears scored 59 points, and Loveland still managed zero catches and zero fantasy points. I'll give Sam that one—that's some cursed bullshit.

Congrats, Sam: you're the first CPBFFL owner to break 25,000 career points. You're at 25,049.70. That's a huge fucking milestone, even if this week's RB2 choice turned the celebration into another loss.

But Blake Corum's 5 over Kyle Monangai's 25? That's on you. Use the real, unrounded points and that one switch gives Sam a 148.06–138.55 win. Instead, Reid beats him again because Sam left the answer sitting on the fucking bench.

2.notes:
CPBFFL ICYMI — WEEK 2

Steve scored the most. Reid scored the least. Mike dropped 162 and somehow walked away 0–2. Sam produced the lowest winning score of the week, while John delivered the biggest ass-kicking. The preseason rankings are already catching fire, and half the league appears to be managed by people using oven mitts.

Shawn Smutak|Brian Corrigan.title: GAME OF THE WEEK: OLAVE THIS WIN, NABERS CAN'T SAVE YOU
Shawn Smutak|Brian Corrigan.body:
Shawn 113.04, Brian 106.51 | Shawn leads the H2H series 10–7 | Both teams are 1–1

Brian got 35 from Amon-Ra and 29 from Dak, which should have been enough to win most weeks. Instead, Malik Nabers scored 1, Jacksonville's defense went negative, and three other starters failed to reach six. Two studs tried dragging six corpses across the finish line and came up short.

Shawn wasn't exactly dominant. Jefferson scored 8, Jameson 5 and Dobbins 3. But Olave scored 22, Diggs added 21, Hampton gave him 17 and Tyler Warren put up 14. It was not pretty, but Shawn had fewer useless assholes in his lineup.

Minnesota's defense scored 21 on Shawn's bench while Tampa scored 4. That decision made this far more stressful than it needed to be, but a win is a win. Shawn takes the Game of the Week, moves to 1–1 and extends his historical edge over Brian.

Reid Masters|John DeBrouse.title: CEEDEE YA LATER, INJURYAPOLIS FLATLINES
Reid Masters|John DeBrouse.body:
John 114.07, Reid 72.95 | Historical H2H tied 3–3 | John moves to 2–0; Reid falls to 1–1

John delivered the biggest blowout of Week 2, beating Reid by 41.12. CeeDee scored 35 and did most of the heavy lifting while Coker and Watson added 14 each. Drake Maye scored only 7, but John could have started a traffic cone at quarterback and still won comfortably.

Reid finished with the lowest score in the league. DJ Moore went negative, Goedert scored 1, Jeremiyah Love scored 7 and the entire lineup produced only four double-digit performances. This wasn't Injuryapolis. This was a fucking morgue.

The bench makes it worse. Jonah Coleman scored 14, Josh Downs scored 14 and Juwan Johnson scored 10. Starting those three over Love, Moore and Goedert adds more than 30 points—and Reid still loses. That's how thoroughly John beat his ass.

Paul Deutsch|Erik Mannarino.title: DART MISFIRES, CRUISERS FINALLY LEAVE PORT
Paul Deutsch|Erik Mannarino.body:
Erik 106.63, Paul 79.60 | Erik leads the H2H series 8–5 | Both teams are 1–1

Paul climbed to No. 2 in the power rankings and immediately scored the second-lowest total of the week. Jaxson Dart scored less than one point. Jayden Reed scored 1. Tucker Kraft, Jakobi Meyers and Rhamondre all scored 3. Ja'Marr Chase put up 26 and basically spent Sunday screaming for someone—anyone—to help him.

Meanwhile, Brock Purdy scored 28 on Paul's bench. Purdy over Dart alone makes this a game. Instead, Paul watched his Monday-night comeback die before it ever had a fucking pulse.

Erik didn't need greatness. Jonathan Taylor scored 29, McBride and the Rams defense each scored 18, and everybody else simply avoided becoming Jaxson Dart. After being the Week 1 punching bag, the Cruisers get off the dock and Erik extends his historical lead over Paul.

Matt Rennert|Tony Yokiel.title: DAVANTE'S INFERNO BURNS THE PRESEASON CHAMP
Matt Rennert|Tony Yokiel.body:
Tony 153.16, Matt 121.48 | Historical H2H tied 1–1 | Both teams are 1–1

So much for Matt being crowned after one week. Tony—the same asshole who scored the third-lowest total in Week 1—came back with the second-highest score in Week 2 and beat the preseason favorite by more than 31.

Davante Adams exploded for 39, DeVonta Smith scored 27, Kenneth Walker added 24 and Kittle put up 18. Puka gave Tony a zero from the bench, and it did not matter. Tony even left Tre Tucker's 23 and Denzel Boston's 23 on the bench because apparently 153 points wasn't obnoxious enough.

Matt got 29 from Goff, 23 from Gibbs and 16 from Garrett Wilson, but Montgomery scored 4 and Michael Mayer scored 5 while Rashod Bateman's 21 sat on the bench. Matt remains dangerous, but the Week 1 coronation lasted exactly seven days before Tony shoved the crown up his ass.

Steve Cegelka|Michael Clark.title: JSN AND THE 176-POINT FUCK-YOU
Steve Cegelka|Michael Clark.body:
Steve 176.18, Mike 162.37 | Steve leads the H2H series 3–2 | Steve moves to 2–0; Mike falls to 0–2

This was the highest-scoring matchup of Week 2, and Steve dropped a league-best 176 despite getting only 7 from Justin Herbert. JSN went nuclear for 45, New England's defense scored 27, Kelce added 25, Waddle scored 21 and Henry gave him 17. When your quarterback shits the bed and you still lead the league in scoring, your roster is doing something right.

Mike scored 162—the third-highest total of the entire week—and lost by almost 14. Josh Allen scored 41, CMC and Kincaid each scored 22, and six starters reached double digits. There was no bad lineup decision to blame. Mike got nearly everything possible from his roster and still got punched in the mouth.

Mike is now 0–2 despite scoring 281.93 points, the second-most in the league. He has also allowed a league-high 327.97. That's not bad management; that's the fantasy gods breaking into his house and taking a shit on the carpet. Steve moves to 2–0 and takes the historical series lead.

Sam Young|Jake Stacy.title: SAM BARELY COOKS, JAKE STILL STARVES
Sam Young|Jake Stacy.body:
Sam 85.17, Jake 81.30 | Sam leads the H2H series 14–4 | Sam moves to 1–1; Jake falls to 0–2

What an absolute sewage leak of a matchup. Sam posted the lowest winning score of Week 2, Jake produced the third-lowest score, and somehow one of these teams had to be rewarded with a victory.

James Cook scored 21 and Parker Washington added 16 for Sam. After that, the lineup became a collection of single-digit disappointments. Caleb scored 6, Loveland scored 1 and Baltimore's defense managed 4. Sam didn't cook shit—he microwaved leftovers and survived.

Jake got 17 from LaPorta, 14 from Lamar and 12 each from Achane and Rice. Wan'Dale scored 1, Addison scored 4 and Croskey-Merritt scored 5. There wasn't a hidden winning lineup on the bench; the whole roster was just bad.

Sam wins the week's narrowest matchup by 3.87 and extends his ridiculous historical advantage to 14–4. Jake is 0–2, dead last in the standings and already making the McGibblets look like expired meat.

1.notes:
WEEK 1 PREDICTIONS — RECALIBRATED

The schedule is out, team names have changed and the defense rules have been rebuilt because Sleeper cannot apply negative scoring only after 10 points or 300 yards. Under the new setup, defenses are no longer handed free points for simply existing. Points allowed are penalized continuously, yardage penalties begin at 300, and impact plays—sacks, turnovers, tackles for loss, passes defended, three-and-outs and fourth-down stops—matter more. That pulls most defenses into a tighter range and makes one touchdown or one complete defensive collapse capable of swinging a matchup.

These are SRS-style fantasy projections using the current starting lineups, the updated CPBFFL scoring, Week 1 player expectations and matchup context. Week 1 is still calibration mode, so everyone may begin preparing their excuses now.

TEAM 3 VS. YOKIEL — Pick: Tony Yokiel, 120.3–118.0. Tony finally dropped The Bye Week name, apparently hoping a rebrand would make everyone forget that he drafted Houston’s defense 100th overall. It did not. Puka projects as the biggest player in this matchup at roughly 20.5, with Hurts around 18.8. Steve answers with JSN near 19.7, Derrick Henry and Bucky Irving, plus enough tight ends to survive a position apocalypse that is not happening. New defensive scoring slightly favors New England over Houston, but not enough to save Steve. Tony wins a close one and immediately acts like the defense reach was genius.

VRABELS LLC VS. SPEAKSOONSTAYLUCKY — Pick: Matt Rennert, 125.9–123.2. This may be the best Week 1 matchup that did not receive the Game of the Week label. Mike brings Josh Allen, Christian McCaffrey, Kyren Williams, Tee Higgins and DK Metcalf. Matt counters with Gibbs, Bowers, Garrett Wilson, Brian Thomas Jr. and enough depth to survive an actual injury. McCaffrey and Gibbs both project above 21 points, so this could become a heavyweight fight quickly. Denver’s defense takes a little more punishment under the revised rules than Seattle, giving Matt another small edge. The village idiot escapes by fewer than three.

DOUBLE DRAKE VS. MCGIBBLETS MUNCHKIN GUILD — Pick: John DeBrouse, 118.7–118.4. Yes, that says John. No, the model has not been hacked. The old projection leaned Jake; the updated scoring turns this into a virtual coin flip and gives John the edge by approximately three-tenths of a point. Lamar and Achane are the two scariest players in the game, but John has CeeDee Lamb, Drake London, Drake Maye and the slightly better defensive projection with the Chargers. Jake still leads the historical series 6-5 and will absolutely claim fraud if he loses by a defensive pass breakup. This is the Upset Special.

INJURYAPOLIS COLTS VS. YOURDADD — Pick: Reid Masters, 119.4–113.8. Bijan is the highest projection in this matchup at roughly 21.7, and Reid has the more complete lineup from top to bottom. Sam still has Cook, Chase Brown, Caleb Williams and enough young talent to make this uncomfortable—but he currently has no defense selected. Under the revised scoring, an average Week 1 defense projects around four to seven points, so filling that spot could turn this into a near toss-up. Until then, Reid owns the roster edge, the model edge and a 3-0 historical record against Sam. The former final boss is once again fighting with one hand tied behind his back, except this time he tied it himself.

GAME OF THE WEEK — COMMISSIONER STILL SUCKS VS. SUNDAY CRUISERS — Pick: Erik Mannarino, 116.7–114.4. The defending champion faces the #2 post-draft team in a Central Division heavyweight fight. Brian gets a major defensive-scoring advantage: Jacksonville projects near 7.7 while the Rams sit around 4.2. Amon-Ra also carries the highest individual expectation in the matchup at roughly 19.8. Erik still has the safer overall build with Burrow, Jonathan Taylor, Saquon and Trey McBride. Brian’s rookies give him the bigger explosion range, but Erik has fewer ways for the entire lineup to shit itself at once. Brian leads the career series 10-7; Erik gets Week 1 by a field goal or less.

LITTLE DOWNIES VS. DEUTSCH4988 — Pick: Paul Deutsch, 125.7–119.3. The corrected 2025 history now shows Paul winning last season, because apparently ruining my week is not a hobby for him—it is a documented tradition. Chase and Nico Collins give Paul two elite projection anchors, while Jaxson Dart only needs to avoid setting the quarterback position on fire. Shawn has Jayden Daniels, Justin Jefferson, Olave and two rookie running backs with real ceiling, but Pittsburgh’s defense carries a modest Week 1 edge over Minnesota under the new rules. The revised model cuts the old projected margin from roughly ten to about six. That is close enough for hope, which is exactly how Paul prefers to make the eventual disappointment hurt.

2026 FINAL STANDINGS & CHAMPION PREDICTION

This forecast blends roster strength, current starter projections, depth, the 14-week schedule, revised defensive scoring and a 20,000-season SRS-style simulation. Matt and Reid draw the friendliest schedules among the contenders. Steve, Tony, Brian and Sam face the roughest paths. This is not a promise; it is simply the computer volunteering to become the next league member everyone can tell to go fuck itself.

1. VRABELS LLC — Matt Rennert — PROJECTED CHAMPION. The deepest roster, the strongest Week 1 projection and approximately a 36% title chance. If Gibbs and Bowers stay healthy, Matt may become completely unbearable.

2. DEUTSCH4988 — Paul Deutsch. Chase, Nico, Breece and Flowers create a massive weekly ceiling. Approximately an 18% title chance, plus a 100% chance Paul gets sniped immediately before at least one waiver claim.

3. INJURYAPOLIS COLTS — Reid Masters. Bijan gives Reid the safest foundation in the league, and the schedule helps. Roughly a 10% title chance. Seniority continues to mean absolutely nothing to him.

4. SPEAKSOONSTAYLUCKY — Michael Clark. Allen and McCaffrey can drag this roster into the championship conversation by themselves. Roughly an 8% title chance. The entire forecast depends on CMC’s body remaining attached.

5. SUNDAY CRUISERS — Erik Mannarino. Taylor, Saquon, Burrow and McBride may be the league’s best starting core. Roughly a 7% title chance, with enough depth to outperform this ranking.

6. MCGIBBLETS MUNCHKIN GUILD — Jake Stacy. Lamar, Achane and A.J. Brown make Jake dangerous every week. Roughly a 6% title chance. The roster is a contender; the owner remains the largest security vulnerability.

7. LITTLE DOWNIES — Shawn Smutak. Strong starters, dangerous rookies and almost no margin for injury. Roughly a 5% title chance. The model predicts another year of researching everything except how to win the final game.

8. COMMISSIONER STILL SUCKS — Brian Corrigan. The defending champion has enormous rookie upside but one of the tougher schedules. Roughly a 3% title chance. If Jeanty, Judkins and Nabers all hit, this ranking will look idiotic by October.

9. YOKIEL — Tony Yokiel. Puka and Hurts keep Tony alive, but the depth and schedule are less forgiving. Roughly a 3% title chance. Changing the team name does not erase the defense pick.

10. DOUBLE DRAKE — John DeBrouse. CeeDee, London and Maye give John a real weekly path. Roughly a 2% title chance. The model likes him more than the league does, which is the lowest possible bar.

11. TEAM 3 — Steve Cegelka. Good starters, useful depth and the hardest projected schedule in the league. Roughly a 2% title chance. If the league unexpectedly changes to three starting tight ends, move Steve directly to number one.

12. YOURDADD — Sam Young. Cook and Chase Brown are good; the roster still needs help and the schedule offers none. Less than a 1% title chance. Sam may remain the career wins leader, but the model sees the castle continuing to crumble.

CHAMPION: MATT RENNERT — VRABELS LLC. Congratulations to Matt on winning a championship that currently exists only inside a simulation. I am sure he will celebrate it with the restraint and humility for which he is famous.

2.notes:
WEEK 2 PREDICTIONS

GAME OF THE WEEK — 6TH LITTLE DOWNIES VS. 3RD COMMISSIONER STILL SUCKS
H2H History: Shawn leads the series 9–7

We get immediate action Thursday night with Jameson Williams and Amon-Ra St. Brown fighting over the same Detroit touchdowns. Brian has the safer side with Amon-Ra, but Shawn only needs one Jameson bomb to wipe that advantage away.

The real fight comes Sunday afternoon. Jayden Daniels and Stefon Diggs give Shawn a stack against Dallas, while Brian sends Dak Prescott out from the opposite sideline. Every Daniels touchdown helps Shawn, but every Dak answer punches right back. Shawn has the better roster from top to bottom this week, especially with Tampa's defense getting Cleveland while Brian is stuck starting Jacksonville's defense in Denver.

Brian's lifeline is Malik Nabers on Monday night. If Shawn handles business Sunday, Nabers should need roughly 20 points to steal it. He'll make Brian sweat it out until the end, but asking Nabers to clean up the entire mess is too much.

Shawn takes the Game of the Week and extends his series lead, 124–116.

4TH INJURYAPOLIS COLTS VS. 5TH DOUBLE DRAKE
H2H History: Reid leads the series 3–2

This is probably the deepest matchup of the week. There isn't one massive mismatch carrying either side; both teams can score from damn near every spot in the lineup.

John's Dallas combination gives him serious upside with CeeDee Lamb attached to the same game as Reid's George Pickens. Reid answers with a more balanced lineup and fewer spots that look ready to completely shit the bed.

This one should remain alive heading into Monday night. Reid will have Cam Skattebo projected for about 13, while John counters with Isaiah Likely projected around nine. If John enters Monday with a small lead, he has a chance. If he is already trailing, Likely probably isn't the guy dragging his ass back.

Reid survives another close matchup and pushes his series lead to 4–2, 126–117.

2ND TEAM DEUTSCH4988 VS. 10TH SUNDAY CRUISERS
H2H History: Erik leads the series 7–5

The rankings say Paul should handle this. The projections say these two assholes are practically even.

Paul has the stronger receiving group, but starting Pittsburgh's defense against New England could erase part of that advantage. Erik also gets Baker Mayfield against his former team, and Saquon Barkley and Jonathan Taylor give him the safer backfield.

The best part is Monday night. Paul has Jaxson Dart starting directly against Erik's Rams defense. Erik should carry a lead into the final game, but every Dart touchdown destroys points from the defense trying to protect it. Paul will likely need around 16 from Dart to finish the comeback, which is almost exactly where he projects.

Erik spends the entire night watching his lead slowly get strangled by the quarterback playing against his own defense.

Paul completes the Monday-night comeback and escapes, 119–115.

1ST VRABELS LLC VS. 12TH THE BYE WEEK
H2H History: Matt leads the series 1–0

Matt starts Thursday night with Jared Goff and Jahmyr Gibbs. That combination projects for more than 40 points, so Tony could be staring at a giant fucking hole before Sunday even begins.

Tony does have a legitimate comeback path. Jalen Hurts and DeVonta Smith give him a stack against Tennessee, Kenneth Walker keeps him alive on Sunday night, and Puka Nacua and Davante Adams wait for the Giants on Monday. Puka and Adams project for approximately 32 combined, meaning Tony will almost certainly enter Monday with a chance.

The problem is Matt's roster is loaded enough to build a lead without needing anybody Monday night. Tony may need closer to 40 from his Rams receivers, which turns a possible comeback into desperation.

Tony makes it look interesting late, but Matt remains No. 1 and moves to 2–0, 134–121.

9TH TEAM 3 VS. 7TH TEAM SPEAKSOONSTAYLUCKY
H2H History: Series tied 2–2

Mike kicks off Week 2 by throwing nearly his entire Buffalo passing attack onto the field Thursday night. Josh Allen, Dalton Kincaid and Khalil Shakir project for roughly 44 combined points. If Buffalo's offense gets rolling, Steve could be getting his ass kicked before he even sets his Sunday lineup.

Steve has enough depth to fight back. Justin Herbert gets Las Vegas, Derrick Henry gets New Orleans, and JSN remains the best player on the roster. Travis Kelce gives Steve another chance to close the gap Sunday night.

Unfortunately, even if Steve survives all of that, Mike still has Kyren Williams waiting against the Giants on Monday. Steve needs to enter Monday with the lead because giving Kyren a reasonable comeback number is asking to lose.

Mike wins the rubber match and takes the series lead, 128–123.

8TH LET'S COOK!! VS. 11TH MCGIBBLETS MUNCHKIN GUILD
H2H History: Sam leads the series 13–4

This matchup begins Thursday with James Cook against Sam LaPorta. Cook has the stronger projection, giving Sam the first chance to grab control.

Then we get the dumbest fantasy battle of the week: Jake starts Lamar Jackson directly against Sam's Baltimore defense. Every Lamar touchdown helps Jake while simultaneously beating the shit out of Sam's defense. Sam needs Baltimore to dominate New Orleans without Lamar being responsible for all the damage, which is a pretty uncomfortable way to spend Sunday.

Jake has Rashee Rice on Sunday night, but Sam gets the final player of the entire matchup with Blake Corum on Monday. The projections have these teams separated by less than one point, so Corum could realistically enter Monday needing around 10 to complete the comeback.

That is a miserable way for Jake to lose, which makes it the most likely outcome.

Sam survives Lamar, gets the Monday-night finish and extends his ridiculous advantage over Jake, 116–113.
